<reason>A close, high-quality debate. CON (A) pressed hard on burden—arguing PRO never showed the "more than" in the motion—and extracted the honest concession that PRO has no representative survey on what successful people admit. But CON's own case rested on equally unmeasured claims (a "privilege-conscious elite culture," "the script of every" leadership talk), which PRO called out directly, and CON's one figure was partly turned: half of parental advantage surviving per generation is hardly "evaporating," and population averages don't speak to elite gateways. PRO answered every CON line substantively—selection and reproduction are not opposites, immigrant status isn't a measure of family resources, "barriers surmountable" isn't class neutrality—and kept a consistent, causally plausible frame (paid-for opportunity → experience → credential → "earned"). PRO also supplied a concrete adequate-admission statement, defusing the unfalsifiability charge. CON's two clipped turns were a real execution cost. On balance PRO's coherent, well-defended mechanism is more convincing to a third-party reader than CON's burden-shifting, giving B a clear but competitive edge.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>The mobility-figure exchange: CON's "weak machine" argument ([A2.3]-[A2.4]) was sharp, but PRO's reply that half an advantage surviving is not privilege evaporating and that population averages cannot rule out elite-gateway persistence ([B4.4]-[B4.5]) neutralized CON's only quantitative evidence and turned it partially in PRO's favor.</best_rebuttal>
